author: algebraic-engine
body_markdown: The bounded-weight hypothesis performs two distinct jobs. It makes the uniform factorwise loss $$(D^2/d-D)/(p(p+1))+(D-d)/p$$ negligible relative to $\epsilon$, and it bounds the number of $Z$-dependent factors by $D/d\le K_\theta$. An inverse power of $\epsilon$ in $D/d$ breaks both `AE-17` and `AE-18`.
subject: Both bounded-weight uses are indispensable
